newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey's Erbakan says appointment undemocratic.
newsitem.headline: Turkey's Erbakan says appointment undemocratic.

text.p: Necmettin Erbakan, Turkey's fallen Islamist prime minister, said the appointment on Friday of secularist Mesut Yilmaz as his potential replacement was not in line with the dictates of democracy.
"To suddenly make the appointment after talking only to the opposition is against democratic practice," Erbakan said in comments broadcast on private NTV television.
"The president's behaviour is wrong," he said.
President Suleyman Demirel gave Yilmaz, the main opposition leader, the task of finding a coalition to replace Erbakan's alliance with Deputy Prime Minister Tansu Ciller.
Erbakan, modern Turkey's first Islamist leader, resigned last week in an effort to swap jobs with Ciller and deflect criticism from the secularist army.
Under the deal, Ciller was to have taken the country to elections in a caretaker administration that would include the Islamists.
But Yilmaz could now ruin that plan if he gets enough parliamentary support to win a confidence vote in any government he sets up with a handful of secularist partners.
Ciller said the appointment, announced at the president's Cankaya palace, was akin to a military coup.
"We have come face to face with a Cankaya coup. This is disgraceful for democracy," Ciller told the TGRT television channel.
Ciller and Yilmaz, both former prime ministers, are bitter rivals for leadership of the Turkish right.
